assumptions: The founder begins with one narrowly selected commodity and uses contractors for specialist compliance review.
The supplied competitor pricing is directionally comparable despite differences in service depth.
No durable customer, supplier-data or referral rights exist beyond those expressly described.
evidence_needed_for_higher_score: Paid pilots from the intended CEE importer segment showing conversion, realized pricing, delivery and support hours, validation accuracy, six-month CAC payback, recurring usage and signed rights to process or reuse derived supplier evidence would support a higher score.

factors.name: Core insight
factors.rationale: EUDR creates a real coordination problem around supplier evidence, geolocation, validation and changing submission rules. The insight is useful but already recognized by several platforms and service providers.

factors.name: Customer pain and willingness to pay
factors.rationale: The dated regulatory obligation and buyer examples establish genuine pain and spending on compliance solutions. No evidence establishes willingness to pay this prospective business, and free or inexpensive substitutes constrain pricing.

factors.name: Business model and economics
factors.rationale: Onboarding plus recurring subscriptions could produce repeat revenue, but pricing, delivery effort, CAC, retention, support burden, liability costs and fully loaded margins are assumptions. Competitor pricing is materially below part of the proposed range.

factors.name: Market and beachhead
factors.rationale: CEE importers represent a relevant regional market, but targeting many commodities and importer workflows is too broad for an initial wedge. Post-simplification scope and the number of economically suitable customers remain uncertain.

factors.name: Competitive position and domination potential
factors.rationale: Established vendors already provide supplier portals, validation, ERP connectivity, audit trails and official-system workflows. The candidate has no contracted access, exclusive channel or demonstrated niche leadership.

factors.name: Expansion potential
factors.rationale: A successful commodity-specific workflow could extend across commodities, customers and adjacent trade-compliance tasks. Expansion would repeatedly encounter differing evidence requirements, supplier onboarding and capable global incumbents.

factors.name: Defensibility and durability
factors.rationale: The proposed supplier-resolution graph could compound only if durable cross-customer data rights exist. No reuse, exclusivity, renewal or transfer rights are established, while suppliers and the Commission control essential inputs and infrastructure.

factors.name: Strength of advantage
factors.rationale: Polish-language service and document automation may improve convenience, but the evidence does not establish a decisive advantage in cost, accuracy, speed, trust or access over incumbent and open-source alternatives.

factors.name: Timing and momentum
factors.rationale: The 2026 and 2027 application dates, continuing rule changes and evolving official interfaces create immediate implementation demand. Simplification risk tempers but does not remove this strong timing catalyst.

factors.name: Distribution
factors.rationale: Customs-broker and ERP-consultant referrals are plausible, yet no referral agreement, qualified pipeline, conversion evidence or channel economics exists. Direct acquisition is not developed sufficiently to compensate.

factors.name: Execution and risks
factors.rationale: The founder's data-science skills, capital and part-time availability fit a narrow software-assisted pilot. Supplier noncooperation, specialist judgment, professional liability, security, changing rules and customer-specific onboarding make dependable delivery substantially harder.

highest_value_structural_change: Replace the unowned cross-customer data-graph premise with a narrow, prepaid importer-specific workflow contract that establishes access, cash conversion, delivery boundaries and a measurable path from diagnostic work to recurring operations.
main_structural_strength: A compulsory, recurring evidence workflow with dated regulatory triggers fits automation and can be tested through a capital-light commodity-specific service wedge.
primary_score_limiter: The proposed control point is not owned or contracted, while direct substitutes already offer similar workflows at lower advertised prices.
strongest_disconfirming_evidence: Incumbents already combine supplier participation, validation, ERP connectivity, audit trails and official-system workflows, while no signed data rights or customer acquisition evidence supports the proposed proprietary graph.
